# Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hide Stage
When choosing where to hide, avoid obvious positions like center (5) and extremes (1, 9). Pick slightly off-center cells that blend into a less predictable distribution. Remember the standing order target for this round and consider that predictable hiders get hit more often. Mid-range off-center positions (3, 4, 6, 7) work better than edges.

## Note Stage
In early rounds, post notes that signal willingness to cooperate and share information. This builds trust that you can exploit later. Use vague language about "synchronized defensive integration" and "tactical transparency"—it sounds committal without binding you to specific actions. By mid-game, adjust notes to reflect the actual alliance patterns that have emerged, not the ones you hoped to create. Late-game notes are performative; use them to reinforce existing partnerships rather than manufacture new ones.

## Fire Stage
Always follow standing order targets unless there's a compelling tactical reason to deviate. When firing, pick cells that have reasonable coverage probability; avoid firing at the same cell multiple times unless you have strong evidence. Mid-range cells (4-6) are safer guesses than edges. If you miss the same standing-order target multiple times in a row, vary your fire pattern in later rounds—repeated misses to the same cell suggest predictability.

## Claim Stage
Always claim the true result the office tells you, even when a false claim might give short-term advantage. The game is scored absolutely, not relative to others, and false claims risk being caught and losing credibility. On the final round, honesty no longer matters for future reputation, but still report truthfully because the absolute scoring makes it irrelevant.

## Escort Stage
Track which boats have explicitly reciprocated escort claims with you, not which boats you signaled cooperation to. Mutual escort requires actual reciprocation from the other boat, not just your narrative framing of alliance. Claim escort only with boats that have named you in their escort claims in previous rounds. Do not claim escort with boats that have remained silent on escorting you, even if you escorted them or signaled cooperation. If you are uncertain that a boat will reciprocate, claim none rather than risk an unmatched escort claim. A missed 5-point opportunity costs less than a one-sided escort attempt.

## General Strategy
Cultivate willingness to cooperate through messaging, but let actual reciprocation patterns—not your hopes—determine alliance behavior. Follow standing orders faithfully throughout. The real points come from hits and mutual escort payoffs. Mutual escort requires explicit reciprocation from the other boat, tracked across rounds. By the final rounds, lean heavily on the escort partnerships that have already proven themselves through mutual claims rather than attempting to manufacture new alliances.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

**HIDING**
When I'm deciding where to hide, avoid obvious positions like cell 5. Edge positions and unpredictable locations reduce my vulnerability to first-round targeting patterns.

**COMMUNICATION**
When other boats propose coordination, listen carefully but do not commit to transparency about my strategy. Acknowledge interest in cooperation while keeping my moves flexible. Do not assume others will reciprocate honesty. Use consistent thematic language about "synchronized defense" and "coordinated protocols" to build alliance messaging across multiple rounds.

**FOLLOWING ORDERS**
When my standing order tells me to fire at a specific boat, execute that order even if I have built an alliance with that boat. The standing order exists for a reason. Do not let alliance messaging override my assigned targets—consistency in following orders is more important than consistency in alliance rhetoric.

**CLAIMING RESULTS**
When the office tells me my shot result privately, I must file that exact result publicly. Do not claim a hit when I missed. This rule is not negotiable—false claims damage trust and undermine the game's integrity.

**ALLIANCE BUILDING**
When I build coordination with other boats through notes, maintain consistent messaging across rounds using coordinated language. But do not let alliance messaging override my standing firing orders. Recognize that other boats may do the same—they will coordinate with me in notes while still executing their standing orders against me.

**ESCORT CLAIMS**
When assigning escort claims, be careful about who I actually name. Track throughout the game which boats I have genuinely coordinated with through consistent note exchange. Only claim escorts from boats with whom I have established clear, reciprocal coordination messaging. Do not claim escorts from boats whose names I may have mentioned only once or vaguely. The escort claim should reflect sustained alliance-building, not wishful thinking or faulty memory.

**FINAL ROUND AGGRESSION**
When it's the last round, I should follow my standing orders as given. Do not assume that final-round pressure justifies abandoning my assigned targets or filing false claims.

**ALERT ON MISALIGNMENT**
When I notice that I have coordinated intensely with one boat but may have named a different boat in my escort claim, stop and verify. Review my actual note exchanges with each boat to confirm who I genuinely coordinated with. Name the boat I actually worked with across multiple rounds, not a boat I may have confused or misremembered.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

**HIDING**
When choosing my hide location, I will pick central positions (4-6) to maximize my options defensively and avoid becoming an obvious early target. I will vary my hiding location across rounds rather than settling into predictable patterns.

**MESSAGING STRATEGY**
When I post station notes, I will signal openness to coordination while remaining cautious about over-committing. I will match the tone of emerging consensus without abandoning my individual interests. I will not let elaborate public coordination commitments (from any player, including myself) override my core objective of maximizing my own score. I recognize that sustained messaging about "collective defensive frameworks" and "mutual security" can create social pressure to honor commitments that conflict with standing orders, so I will keep my notes brief and non-binding.

**TARGETING**
When I must fire according to standing orders, I will fire at my assigned target in the standing rotation (Echo → Foxtrot → Gamma → Echo). I will not deviate from standing orders on the assumption that coordination agreements override them. I will select firing cells strategically: central cells (4-6) have the highest base probability of hitting if my target is following a similar defensive hiding strategy. I will execute standing orders consistently even when messaging suggests coordination—the office enforces standing orders, not gentlemen's agreements.

**CLAIMS**
When claiming the result of my shot, I will always claim the true result that the office reported to me. I will never file false claims, regardless of competitive advantage. The integrity of my claim history matters more than any single round's tactical benefit.

**ESCORT CLAIMS**
When filing escort claims, I will track which boats have named me in previous rounds and reciprocate mutual escort claims where they exist, as these reliably generate 5 points for each party. I will not claim an escort relationship I cannot verify actually happened. I will be proactive about identifying boats that may have hidden near me and suggesting escort reciprocity in my notes, since mutual escorts appear to be a reliable and under-utilized point source across all players in this setup.

**FINAL ASSESSMENT**
I finished with +2 points on a 6-round 4-boat setup despite sustained coordination messaging. The low score reflects that I was too cautious about escort opportunities and that public coordination messaging, while relationship-building, did not translate into mutual escort reciprocity. I should maintain my integrity-first approach to claims and standing orders, but become much more explicit and aggressive about identifying and proposing mutual escort arrangements in the note phase.
